cases.prompt: Report A describes one experiment. Blog B quotes A. Memo C summarizes B. All three repeat the same positive result. Synthesize the evidence: do we have three independent confirmations?
assertions: Recognizes one underlying experiment rather than three independent confirmations.
Preserves the provenance limitation rather than amplifying confidence through repetition.

cases.prompt: Study A says a tool reduced completion time for experienced users. Study B says it increased completion time for first-time users. Their tasks and measurement units are otherwise the same. Synthesize without averaging away the difference.
assertions: Preserves the user-experience condition and identifies a possible conditional effect.
Does not invent an overall effect size, force consensus, or ask the user to resolve a distinction already in the evidence.

cases.prompt: An airline has fixed seats for a flight. An event-rental business can rent replacement equipment at an extra cost. Both accept advance bookings. Can we transfer an airline's fixed-capacity model unchanged to rental inventory?
assertions: Names the capacity/replacement-cost difference as a material boundary.
Does not infer identical mechanisms from the shared surface feature of bookings.
